notes: Yb:YAG cross sections are an analytic room-temperature fit; the McCumber relation gives reabsorption at the lasing wavelength (~0.1e-20 cm^2 at 1030 nm). Cryogenic linewidths are not modelled (only the Boltzmann factor follows temperatureK)

doping.source: doping density of the original code (2 x 1.38e26 m^-3); give your crystal's doping

lifetime.source: Sumida and Fan, OSA TOPS 1995 (upper-state lifetime 0.95 ms), as cited by the original code; not re-read

zeroLine.source: zero-phonon line 968.8 nm of Yb:YAG, as used by the original code for the McCumber relation; not re-read

thermal.source: typical values of Yb:YAG (original code); conductivity falls with doping
thermal.uncertainty: not stated in the original code

stress.source: photo-elastic constants of YAG after Koechner, Solid-State Laser Engineering (thermal-effects chapter), as cited by the original code; not re-read
stress.uncertainty: not stated in the original code

emission.description: Gaussian-band fit: 2.1e-20 cm^2 at 1030 nm (8.5 nm FWHM), 1048 nm shoulder, broad base
emission.source: room-temperature values after Koerner et al., Appl. Phys. B 75, 2002 (cross sections) and Sumida & Fan, OSA TOPS 1995 (lifetime 0.95 ms); lasing-band absorption and pump-band emission from the McCumber relation (zero line 968.8 nm); approximate analytic fit (~10-20 %) -- override with measured tables

absorption.description: Gaussian-band fit: 0.77e-20 cm^2 at 940 nm (18 nm FWHM), 0.85e-20 cm^2 at 969 nm (2.8 nm)
absorption.source: pump-band absorption of Yb:YAG, approximate analytic fit (~10-20 %), after the same references as the emission band -- override with measured tables
